header: Test vectors of type MlDsaVerify are meant for the verification of ML-DSA signatures
Mutation-driven single-defect vectors (vector-forge): each targets one check of FIPS 204 Algorithms 8 and 21.
See doc/mldsa.md for details on how to apply these test vectors.

InvalidContext.description: The context is longer than 255 bytes.

InvalidHintsEncoding.description: The hint section is not a valid HintBitPack output (FIPS 204 Algorithm 21 must return bottom): indices out of order or repeated, counts decreasing or above omega, or non-zero padding. Exactly one defect.

ModifiedContext.description: The context differs from the signed context in one byte, or by one appended, prepended or removed byte, or is empty.

ModifiedMessage.description: The message differs from the signed message in one byte, or by one appended, prepended or removed byte.

ModifiedSignature.description: The signature was obtained by modifying a valid signature (a bit flip, a replaced c-tilde, or an edit of the hint section that is still a valid encoding). Exactly one defect; everything else is valid.

ValidSignature.description: The test vector contains a valid signature.

ModifiedPublicKey.description: The public key was obtained by flipping one bit of the key the signature was made with.

BoundaryCondition.description: The case sits on a boundary of a check or of a rounding function (z at gamma1 - beta - 1 or gamma1 - beta, encoding extremes, UseHint at r0 = 0 / +-1 / +-gamma2 edges or the top-bucket fold, MakeHint borders, Power2Round remainders).

InfinityNormViolation.description: A coefficient of z is at or beyond gamma1 - beta; the verification equation itself holds, so only the infinity-norm check rejects it.

ZeroPublicKey.description: The public key has t1 = 0, so w'approx = A z does not depend on c and the signature can be built with chosen z and hints. This makes it trivial to forge signatures, but that's none of the verification algorithm's business.
